summary: Malformed/invalid JSON responses when quantization enabled on JSON-mode route (structured output regression)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer (FinchAI) reports output format regressions on a JSON-mode route after enabling Quantization Profile Library for cost reduction.
- Symptoms: responses occasionally contain invalid JSON (unterminated strings, trailing commentary, or missing closing braces) despite JSON-mode / structured output prompts.
- Impact: downstream parser failures in production workflow; route is used for programmatic extraction where strict JSON validity is required.

Impact
- Increased application errors due to JSON parse failures.
- Customer reports regression is workload-visible (same prompts previously produced valid JSON at near-100% on baseline fp16/bf16 path).

Environment
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated
- Region: prod us-east
- Route: finchai-prod/extract/v2 (JSON-mode; strict JSON required)
- Models tested: llama-3.1-70b-instruct, qwen2.5-72b-instruct
- Quantization profile: customer enabled Redwood-published int4 profile via route-level setting (100% rollout)
- Customer notes temperature is low (0.1) and they use a strict system prompt.

Steps to reproduce (per customer)
1) Enable quantization on the JSON-mode route in Console (Route Settings -> Quantization -> Enabled).
2) Send extraction requests expecting JSON object output.
3) Observe occasional invalid JSON responses.
4) Disable quantization (set to Disabled / 0% canary) and repeat; invalid JSON occurrences stop.

Observed behavior
- Invalid JSON examples (customer-provided snippets; redacted fields):
  - Example A: "{\n  \"entities\": [ ... ]\n  \"confidence\": 0.82\n" (missing closing brace)
  - Example B: "{\"id\":\"123\",\"status\":\"ok\"}\n\nNote: I assumed ..." (trailing non-JSON text)
  - Example C: "{\"items\":[{\"name\":\"Acme\",\"qty\":2}]}\"" (extra quote at end)

Expected behavior
- Responses must be valid JSON (parseable) as required by route contract.

Redwood investigation notes
- Correlating traces show failures primarily when quantization profile is active (execution_mode=quantized) and not observed on baseline path for the same route.
- No evidence of runtime truncation or streaming disconnects in the failing samples; token counts are within max_tokens, and responses are completed normally.
- Early hypothesis: quantized variant increases "format drift" on strict structured output prompts in this customer’s prompt set (tool/JSON style). This matches known risk area and is explicitly called out in quantization acceptance criteria as requiring prompt-set coverage.

Relevant logs / request IDs (from Redwood telemetry)
- 2025-01-14 09:41:22Z request_id=req_01HTQ8V6M0F2K7A8Q9D7W0K2B3 route=finchai-prod/extract/v2 model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct quant_profile_id=qpl_llama31_70b_int4_v1.2.0 execution_mode=quantized status=200 json_parseable=false
- 2025-01-14 09:43:10Z request_id=req_01HTQ8Y0KJ6EJQ9G8MZ0Z8Z0RX route=finchai-prod/extract/v2 model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct quant_profile_id=qpl_llama31_70b_int4_v1.2.0 execution_mode=baseline status=200 json_parseable=true (customer retried after disabling)

Workaround
- Disable quantization on the JSON-mode route (keep quantization enabled only on non-JSON/background routes).
- Customer confirmed disabling quantization on finchai-prod/extract/v2 resolves parser failures immediately.

Resolution
- Applied mitigation: FinchAI disabled quantization on the impacted JSON-mode route and left quantization enabled on their batch summarization route.
- Redwood action: track as a quantization quality regression in structured output; add this customer prompt shape to quantization validation coverage before re-recommending int4 for JSON-mode routes.

Next steps / follow-ups
- Applied ML / Quality: review the int4 profile’s structured-output prompt-set deltas; consider tightening publish gates for JSON-mode compatibility or adding profile notes/constraints (e.g., "not recommended for strict JSON-mode workloads" until passing additional evals).
- Product/Console: ensure UI warnings for JSON-mode routes are clear ("Quantization may increase structured output format errors; use canary/monitoring").
- Support: provide FinchAI with guidance on safe rollout (start at 1–5% canary, add automatic rollback triggers based on json_parseable rate).
comments: [2025-01-14 10:12 PT] Markus Klein (Reporter): FinchAI seeing invalid JSON outputs when enabling quantization on their extract route (strict JSON-mode). They can reproduce reliably across a few prompt templates. Disabling quantization fixes it. Requesting guidance + whether we can recommend a safer profile/setting.

[2025-01-14 10:27 PT] Selene Huang (Assignee): Acknowledged. This is consistent with structured output being a sensitive area for some quantized variants. Can you share: route_id, model(s), profile_id shown in response headers/route settings, and ~10 sample request_ids that produced invalid JSON? Also confirm if they are using streaming.

[2025-01-14 10:46 PT] Markus Klein: Shared request_ids in ticket description + confirmed non-streaming for this route. Temperature=0.1. They’re using JSON-mode style system prompt (no tool calls, but strict JSON object output).

[2025-01-14 11:30 PT] Logan Wright: Pulled traces for the request_ids. Correlation: json_parseable=false almost exclusively when execution_mode=quantized with qpl_llama31_70b_int4_v1.2.0. No 5xx. Completion looks normal (not cut off). Suggest setting quantization canary to 0% for this route until we can validate structured-output promptset coverage.

[2025-01-14 12:05 PT] Selene Huang: +1. Recommended immediate workaround: disable quantization on JSON-mode route, keep on batch routes. Also suggest adding a runtime-side metric/guardrail for "structured-output validity" if available, but for now customer-side parsing is the right signal.

[2025-01-15 09:18 PT] Markus Klein: FinchAI applied workaround (disabled quantization on extract route; kept it on summarization route). They report JSON parse failures stopped. They want to know if int8 would be safer than int4 for JSON-mode.

[2025-01-15 10:02 PT] Selene Huang: We don’t have a blanket guarantee that int8 fixes structured-output drift, but it often reduces regressions vs int4. However, until the profile passes our JSON-mode prompt set gates for their model family, we should not recommend enabling on strict JSON routes. Best practice: canary 1–5% with monitoring for json_parseable rate and rollback.
Action item on our side: add JSON-mode/structured output prompts to quantization library coverage plan and rerun evals for the relevant profiles.
[2025-01-16 16:40 PT] Markus Klein: Customer satisfied with workaround + safer rollout guidance. Marking ticket resolved. Will follow up if they want to test int8 under a canary later.
